Repair 010 introduces no unacceptable gap closure, fusion, spike, carrier slab, flattening, depth inversion, or collateral wrist damage.

inspected_pairs.observation: The central cuff brace remains a coherent faceted loop/bridge with an open upper aperture, angular ledge, separate flanking plates, and intentional registration against neighboring rails.
The stepped underside, short struts, and horizontal channels remain recognizable and separate without fusion, closure, spike, slab, flattening, or depth reversal.
The beveled cuff face keeps polygonal volume and its long recessed channel remains open; the outward shift exposes negative space without interpenetration, carrier wall, flattening, or inversion.
The cuff shell, inset border, lower tabs, and pre-existing pointed flange retain their visual vocabulary; increased layer separation does not create a new connection or abrupt deformation.

The largest local delta is a substantial outward shift of the cuff and neighboring plate; the opening stays open and pieces remain separate, but assembly-scale evidence is required to judge registration.

At whole-wrist scale the opening, rings, side loops, and layered details remain recognizable; the modest opening-shape change does not read as closure, fusion, slab generation, spike, or depth inversion.
The full dorsal silhouette, long rails, upper-arm mass, elbow openings, wrist cuff, and major negative spaces remain registered without propagated damage.
The ventral outline, circular wrist detail, side cage, lower rails, and elbow separation remain stable without collateral fusion or shell displacement.
Nested wrist rings, circular plates, side cage, hanging rails, open gaps, wrist-to-forearm transition, and separated upper shell remain visually credible.

uncertainty: Source and current use different display colors, reducing sensitivity to extremely subtle shading-only differences.
The local wrist-axial delta is substantial relative to the 19-26 mm detail scale, although it does not read as objectionable at whole-wrist scale.

The affected-edge minimum ratio of 0.506504 represents nearly 49.4 percent contraction; no corresponding visual failure appears in the reviewed views, but the reversible repair should remain a candidate through later structural and physical-detail validation.
The repair leaves 282 global cutter penetrations, 305 reserved-margin violations, and 701 triangle overlaps, so it cannot support fitted-surface promotion.
follow_up: Parent workflow may retain Repair 010 as a reversible candidate and continue with the next bounded easy component.
